title: mut.channel_cosmic_web_filaments
mutation_directive: Cosmic Web — IllustrisTNG / MillenniumTNG filament structure — MillenniumTNG simulation (MPA Garching, 2024); 'Galaxies in the Simulated Cosmic Web' (A&A 2025); NASA Hubble Cosmic Web mapping. VISUAL SIGNATURE: Hundreds-of-millions-of-light-years scale: bright dense nodes (galaxy clusters) connected by long thin filaments of dark matter, with vast empty voids between. Reads as a sparse 3D foam, or a sponge skeleton. Color: black void, golden-orange filaments where gas is dense, magenta clusters; or a more austere blue-on-black per the IllustrisTNG render style. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Generate a 3D Voronoi tessellation of N=200 cells in a cube; place ~50k particles ALONG the Voronoi edges (the filaments) with Gaussian falloff perpendicular to each edge; concentrate dense clumps at the vertices (cluster nodes). Particles drift slowly along the filaments toward nearest node (gravitational infall). Use additive blending; colormap from edge-distance: hot near vertices, cool mid-filament, dark in voids. Camera dolly is at galactic scale — feels vast. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has 0-D point clouds (Lucy), 1-D chains (boids), 2-D fields (waves). This is true 1.5-D Voronoi-edge structure at cosmological scale — a different topological dimension and an entirely new spatial scale (galaxies, not particles). Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://www.mpa-garching.mpg.de/1098309/hl202406
